scopeNote: Old Bangkok by the river: Rattanakosin, Banglamphu and Pratu Phi, Dusit and Nang Loeng, Chinatown and Talat Noi, Charoen Krung and Bang Rak by the old Oriental, and the Thonburi bank (Khlong San, Kudi Chin, Wang Lang), checked against the Michelin Guide Thailand 2026 lists, Wongnai Users' Choice 2026 and Google Maps on 27 Oct 2026.

basics.title: Street food: when stalls cook and how to pay
basics.text: Old Bangkok eats in two shifts: pork-leg, congee and noodle shops cook from about 7:00 and many sell out or close by 13:00-15:00, while Yaowarat and Banglamphu stalls open from about 17:00 to midnight. Monday is the weakest day, because many street vendors and Yaowarat stalls take it off. Most stalls are cash only; many show a Thai QR code (PromptPay) that needs a Thai bank app, so carry small notes (20, 100 THB). At famous stalls you often pay or order before you sit, and the queue moves faster than it looks.

basics.title: Michelin street stalls: is the queue worth it
basics.text: The 2026 Michelin Guide cut many old Chinatown and Bang Rak stalls (Nai Ek, Ouan Pochana, Jok Prince, Prachak are no longer listed), but Thai diners still rate them highly on Wongnai. Bib Gourmand means good value, not a long queue: places such as Krua Apsorn, K. Panich or Kolun.h usually take 0-20 minutes. Jay Fai, the one-star stall, means 2-3 hours of waiting and about 1,500 THB for the crab omelette; most groups are happier at Thipsamai or Fai Ta Lu nearby. Go at opening time or mid-afternoon to avoid the worst queues.

basics.title: Fine dining: booking and dress
basics.text: Book the starred restaurants weeks ahead: Nusara has about 10 seats at one table and Potong about 28, so a table for 8 needs early contact and sometimes a full buyout. Most take bookings on their own site, by phone or LINE, and some ask for a deposit or card guarantee. Prices are shown before 10% service and 7% VAT, so add about 17%. Dress smart casual; at hotel restaurants such as Le Normandie avoid shorts, sandals and sleeveless shirts.

basics.title: Getting around for food
basics.text: The MRT Blue Line is the easiest way in: Wat Mangkon for Yaowarat, Hua Lamphong for Talat Noi and Si Morakot, Sam Yot for Pratu Phi, the Giant Swing and Phraeng Phuthon, and Sanam Chai for Wat Pho and Tha Tien. The Chao Phraya Express boat links Tha Chang, Tha Tien, Ratchawong (Chinatown), Si Phraya, Oriental and Sathorn pier (BTS Saphan Taksin), and small cross-river ferries go to Wang Lang and Wat Arun. For 8 people book two Grab cars or a large car; Chinatown traffic is slow after 17:00, so walk the last part.
